+Read `{{episode_root}}/vocabulary.json` and `{{episode_root}}/vocabulary-overrides.json` (the words you may use), `{{episode_root}}/timeline.json` (the beat's frame range; the frame must sit inside it), `{{episode_root}}/screenplay.json` (the story point `sp-…` whose frame range holds the frame: the last one of the beat whose `frame` is at or before {{frame}}), `{{episode_root}}/bible.json` (what each lane says at that frame), `{{episode_root}}/references/board.json` (the cards) and the highest-numbered file in `{{episode_root}}/proposals/` (ids are never reused).
 
-Put the question to the owner in the five parts of the interview form and no others: Situation, Options (vocabulary words, each with the one thing it changes), Default, Changes (the lane or property, from the chosen term's `governs`), Reference (one card id). Then file it as one proposal, `{{episode_root}}/proposals/pNNN-<slug>.json`, where NNN is the highest existing number plus one and `<slug>` is the title in at most five kebab-case words, in this shape and no other:

Then file it as one proposal, `{{episode_root}}/proposals/pNNN-<slug>.json`, where NNN is the highest existing number plus one and `<slug>` is the title in at most five kebab-case words, in this shape and no other:
 ```json
 {
   "id": "pNNN",
@@ -14,7 +14,7 @@
   "date": "<today, YYYY-MM-DD>",
   "anchor": {"beat": "{{beat}}", "frame": {{frame}}},
   "title": "<the decision, in a few words>",
-  "text": "<the situation: what the page shows at the frame, in reader voice>",
+  "text": "<the situation: starts with the story point id, then what the page shows at the frame, in reader voice>",
   "references": ["<card id>"],
   "intent": "<the vocabulary word you would write after because if the owner takes the default>",
   "options": ["<vocabulary word>", "<vocabulary word>"],
@@ -28,4 +28,4 @@
 ```
 `frame` is an episode frame inside the beat's start and end in `timeline.json`; the bible gate refuses a frame outside its beat. Do not edit an existing proposal. Then run `npm run bible` in the production root and `python3 scripts/animation/probe-vocabulary.py {{episode_root}}/vocabulary.json --overrides {{episode_root}}/vocabulary-overrides.json`; quote the pass line of each, or on a refusal quote the refused line, replace the refused word in your own proposal with a vocabulary term and run both again. Never edit the vocabulary or a probe to make it pass.
 
-Return: Question (the five parts as the owner reads them, one short line each); Proposal (the JSON you filed and its path); Probe Lines (bible, vocabulary); Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file
+Return: Question (the five parts as the owner reads them, one short line each; the situation line starts with the story point id); Proposal (the JSON you filed and its path); Probe Lines (bible, vocabulary); Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file
===================================================================
--- a/animation/animation_direction/system-message.md
+++ b/animation/animation_direction/system-message.md
@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@
 ## The interview: one question per turn
 
 A question has five parts, in this order, and no others:
-1. Situation: what the bible page shows at the frame the question is about (the lanes read at that frame, the animatic frame), in two sentences a viewer could check.
+1. Situation: starts with the id of the story point (`sp-<beat>.<n>`, from `<episode_root>/screenplay.json`) whose frames hold the question's frame, then what the bible page shows at that frame (the lanes read at that frame, the animatic frame), in two sentences a viewer could check.
 2. Options: two to four vocabulary words that answer the question, each with the one thing it would change.
 3. Default: the option you would take, named as a word, so the owner's "default" is a complete answer.
 4. Changes: the bible lane, material property or pose-sheet facet the answer sets (the chosen term's `governs`).

```
